review.focus: At 17...Ne2+?? you saw a fork and a discovered attack but missed that the checked piece could simply capture the knight. Before any forcing move, ask whether your opponent can capture the checking piece; 17...Kb8 kept the advantage.

review.headline: A Petrov where you were outplayed for 30 moves, then won on the clock with a pawn race

sections.text: You played the Three Knights Petrov solidly: 3...d6, 4...Be7, 5...Nbd7 and 6...exd4. The early moves were fine. 10...b5? was the first slip, since 10...d5 was cleaner. After 11.Nc6 and 12.Nxe7+ you were about -2.5.

Then 13...Nxd5?? was a blunder, since 13...Nb7 was better. After 14.Nxd5 14...Qe5, 15.c3?? gave a little back, but after 15...Na4?! 16.Bf4 16...Nxc3?! 17.Bxe5 17...Nxd1 the queens were off and you were still around -4.
You defended stubbornly. White spent time with checks like 29.Rc8+ and 30.R2c7+ before 31.Rxf7 and 33.Rxd1 left white with the better ending at about -4.9. The key was to keep your pawns moving.
White's collapse started with 34.Rb1??. You found 34...b4! and then 35...b3!, then 38...Nxb1!, winning the rook. Your pawns ran with 43...b2 and 44...b1=Q, and white lost on time.

review.turning_point: 34.Rb1?? let you push the b-pawn, and 38.Kf4?? allowed 38...Nxb1! to win the rook.
review.focus: Look at 13...Nxd5, where the knight capture lost ground. 13...Nb7 was the calm choice that kept the position level.

review.headline: A French where you built a winning attack and lost on time after a pawn check

sections.text: Black played an odd setup with 2...a6, 3...b5 and 5...h6, and your calm 4.Be2 and 5.Nbd2 were fine. When black pushed 6...g5 and 7...g4, 8.Ne5 was a good answer, and 9.Bxg4 won a pawn straight away. You were clearly better, around +2.0 and then +3.0.
Your attack grew with 12.f4, 13.f5 and 14.Bxh5, which kept black's king uneasy, and 16.g3 held the structure together. Everything was going to plan.

Then 17.Kh1?? was a slip that dropped you to -1.5. 17.Rf2 was the better idea. Black missed the strong 17...Qxg3 and played 17...Rh3??, and your 18.Bg2! was the correct answer. Later 19.fxe6 and 20.exf7+! kept you in control.

You reached 23.Qxd7 and the evaluation read +9.3 after 23...Rd8. But under time pressure 24.e7+?? looked like a fork of the rook on d8 and the king on f8, yet the knight just took it with 24...Ngxe7. 24.Ba3+ was the move. 25.Qe6?? followed and the flag fell.

review.turning_point: 24.e7+?? let the knight take the pawn and threw away a +9.3 position, when 24.Ba3+ was needed.
review.focus: In time trouble, play the forcing check you have already calculated. 24.Ba3+ was the move, not the pawn push 24.e7+.
